I fetched the page and the quote is on it, word for word. All four parts of the rule are met. But the claim looks like a repeat of one already on file, so my reading is "recorded", with one point a person needs to check.

**The page.** It's a third-party transcript on singjupost.com of Hassabis's All-In Summit interview with David Friedberg. The page dates it 13 September 2025. The quote matches exactly, apart from the curly apostrophe in "that's". It comes right after he says today's systems are "not PhD intelligences" because they aren't consistently capable, and that "a true AGI system" shouldn't make simple mistakes in high-school maths or counting. Since this is a transcript of the interview, not a news report, it counts as a primary source, not coverage.

**The four parts:**
1. **Role:** pass. In September 2025 he was co-founder and chief executive of Google DeepMind.
2. **Looks forward and is about AI:** pass. He says when an AGI system will arrive. "Maybe, I would say sort of" is hedging, not a hypothetical, so it is scored at face value with the hedge kept in the wording.
3. **Date or span:** pass. "Five to 10 years" is a range of spans, so the later end applies: ten years from September 2025, due 2035.
4. **Primary source:** pass. The source is a transcript.

**Why "recorded".** There is already a file for the same forecast: `2025-04-20-hassabis-agi-five-to-ten-years.toml`. Both say AGI in five to ten years, and both come due in 2035. Under the restatement rule, that makes this an unchanged repeat. It should go into that file's `repeated_on` as 2025-09-13, not become a new claim. The May file (`2025-05-23-hassabis-agi-most-mass-five-to-ten-years`) also comes due in 2035, and from its name it appears to cover the same forecast. The Davos 2026 file comes due in 2036, so it is a separate record.

**What to check.** In this interview he defines AGI as a system that works at PhD level consistently, across the board. For a named stage, the test is the definition the speaker gives in the same source. If the April file's test rests on a materially different definition, this could count as a "changed condition". It would then be a new record that names the April claim in `restates`. I didn't open the April file to compare, so this is borderline between "recorded" and "pass".
